style.vernacular: Colonial-planned northern capital (founded 1913 for the Northern Nigeria Protectorate) on the Kaduna River: wide avenues of broadleaf shade trees, Lugard-era government buildings with verandas and red-tiled or corrugated hipped roofs, 1960s-70s regional-government modernist blocks in concrete and cream render, dense Hausa neighbourhoods of mud-render and painted sandcrete compounds, and red laterite ground.
style.ornament: Colonial verandas on slender columns, shuttered or louvred windows and hipped roofs on government buildings; Hausa/Arewa relief patterns, pinnacled parapets and pointed arches on mosques and northern-regional buildings (Lugard Hall is described as echoing emirs' palaces); modernist concrete screens and brise-soleil on 1960s-70s blocks.

sources.what: founded by the British near the Lagos-Kano railway, Lugard Hall, Murtala Square racecourse/polo, tropical savanna Aw climate, ~250 m elevation
colonial-era designs still visible in the government district (secondary travel source)
Lugard Hall thesis: colonial architecture of Northern Nigeria and its preservation
Lugard Hall 1914, resembles emirs' palaces, distinctive dome (commercial listing, cautious)
